# Have you been told you can t get federal student aid any longer?

In most circumstances, there are things you can do to get back your eligibility for financial aid.

You might lose federal student aid eligibility for a number of reasons. For instance, you might no longer meet one of the basic eligibility criteria, or you might have changed majors and no longer be enrolled in a program that makes you eligible to receive a specific type of funding (for instance, a Teacher Education Assistance for College and Higher Education [TEACH] Grant). We recommend you talk to your financial aid office about those and any other circumstances that cause you to lose eligibility.

Meanwhile, below we provide some tips on how to get your eligibility back if you find yourself in one of the following situations:

## What if I defaulted on my student loan but now I want to get more federal student aid?

You ll need to get out of default before you can receive aid again.

## What if my grades slipped, or I haven t completed enough credits, and my financial aid office told me I can t get federal student aid?

You need to make satisfactory academic progress in college or career school in order to keep getting federal student aid. Talk to your school about whether you can appeal the decision that made you ineligible to continue receiving federal student aid.

## What if I was an eligible noncitizen but my status expired or was revoked?

You ll need to reinstate the status that made you an eligible noncitizen, or become a citizen or permanent resident, before you can receive federal student aid. For information about reinstating your status or becoming a citizen, contact U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services.

## What if I was convicted of a drug offense but now I want to get more federal student aid?

If you ve lost eligibility due to a conviction for a drug offense, and you are not scheduled to regain eligibility this academic year, it is possible to regain eligibility early.

## What if I m incarcerated?

Your incarceration affects your eligibility for different types of aid in different ways. If you are ineligible for a particular type of student aid due to your incarceration, you ll need to wait until you re released before you can get that type of aid.

## What if I accidentally received more federal student loan or grant money than I was supposed to?

In certain cases, you ll need to repay the amount that was beyond the maximum that you were allowed to receive. You can either repay the excess all at once, or you can make arrangements to repay it a bit at a time. Once you ve repaid or made arrangements to repay the excess, you ll be able to receive additional federal student aid (assuming you haven t reached the maximum amounts for all programs for which you are otherwise eligible). In other cases, your financial aid office might be able to adjust the amount of money you ll be getting from another federal student aid program to make up for the excess you received. If you have questions about repaying aid or getting additional aid, talk to the financial aid staff at your school.

## What if I thought I had a high school diploma, but it turns out that I actually don t?

This situation might arise if, for instance, your high school is a diploma mill (a school that charges a student a fee and requires him or her to complete little or no course work to get the diploma). If you don t have a high school diploma or an equivalent such as a General Educational Development (GED) certificate, you ll need to talk to the financial aid office at your school to find out what to do.

## What if I was convicted of, or pled nolo contendere or guilty to, a crime involving fraud to obtain federal student aid funds?

You ll need to repay the funds to the U.S. Department of Education or in the case of a federal student loan to the holder or servicer of the loan.

## What if I have property subject to a judgment lien?

If you have property subject to a judgment lien for a debt owed to the United States, you will have to pay your debt in full or make arrangements to pay the debt."}, {"chunk_id": "Reporting Parent Information | Federal Student Aid#1_0::c0007", "text": "[受抚养学生必须在其联邦学生援助免费申请（FAFSA）表格上报告其家长信息以及自己的信息。 > 如果我因特殊情况无法提供父母信息怎么办？]

# Many non-U.S. citizens qualify for federal student aid.

Don t assume you can t get aid just because you re not a citizen.

The most common category of eligible noncitizen is that of permanent resident (someone with a green card ), but there are other categories as well.

## I am a non-U.S. citizen. Can I get federal student aid?

Check with your college or career school s financial aid office for more information. You are considered an eligible noncitizen if you fall into certain categories, such as the ones listed below:

1\. You are a

- U.S. national (includes natives of American Samoa or Swains Island) or
- U.S. permanent resident with a Form I-551, I-151, or I-551C (Permanent Resident Card, Resident Alien Card, or Alien Registration Receipt Card), also known as a "green card."

2\. You have an Arrival-Departure Record (I-94) from U.S. Citizen and Immigration Services (USCIS) showing*

- Refugee,
- Asylum Granted,
- Cuban-Haitian Entrant,
- Conditional Entrant (valid only if issued before April 1, 1980), or
- Parolee (you must be paroled for at least one year, and you must be able to provide evidence from the USCIS that you are in the United States for other than a temporary purpose with the intention of becoming a U.S. citizen or permanent resident).

3\. You hold a T nonimmigrant status ("T-visa") (for victims of human trafficking) or your parent holds a T-1 nonimmigrant status. Your college or career school s financial aid office will ask to see your visa and/or certification letter from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.*

4\. You are a battered immigrant-qualified alien who is a victim of abuse by your citizen or permanent resident spouse, or you are the child of a person designated as such under the Violence Against Women Act (VAWA).*

5\. You are a citizen of the Federated States of Micronesia, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, or the Republic of Palau. If this is the case, you may be eligible for only certain types of federal student aid:

- Citizens of the Republic of Palau are eligible for Federal Pell Grants, Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grants, and Federal Work-Study.
- Citizens of the Federal States of Micronesia and the Republic of the Marshall Islands are eligible for Federal Pell Grants only.

*To qualify for federal student aid, certain eligible noncitizens must be able to provide evidence from the USCIS that they are in the United States for other than a temporary purpose with the intention of becoming a U.S. citizen or permanent resident.

Certain Native American students born in Canada with a status under the Jay Treaty of 1789 may also be eligible for federal student aid.

## If I have been granted Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA), am I eligible for federal student aid?

Undocumented students, including DACA recipients, are not eligible for federal student aid, but you may still be eligible for state or college aid, in addition to private scholarships. Check with your college or career school s financial aid office for more information.

## If I have been granted DACA, should I still complete a FAFSA form?

You should check with your high school counselor or financial aid office to see whether completing the FAFSA form is the way to apply for state and college student aid. To begin your FAFSA form, you must enter your Social Security number. While completing the FAFSA form, you must answer the Are you a U.S. citizen? question as No, I am not a citizen or eligible noncitizen. After submitting your FAFSA form, you should check with your college s financial aid office to see what types of financial aid you may be eligible to receive.

Our fact sheet about undocumented students and financial aid provides more details and tips for DACA recipients filling out the FAFSA form.

## Does my parents citizenship or immigration status affect my eligibility for aid?

No, your parents citizenship or immigration status does not affect your eligibility for federal student aid. In fact, the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form doesn t even ask about your parents status. Learn about filling out the FAFSA form.

## What if the expiration date on my documents has passed?

- If your green card has expired, it doesn t necessarily mean that your status as a legal permanent resident has expired. You might just need to renew the card. Be sure to do so promptly!
- If your permanent residence status has in fact expired, you are no longer eligible for federal student aid.
- If your documentation shows that you are a Cuban-Haitian Entrant, you are still an eligible noncitizen even if the expiration date has passed.
- For all other documents listed in 1 3 above, if the expiration date has passed, you are not an eligible noncitizen and cannot receive federal student aid.

For more information about eligible noncitizen status, contact your college's or career school's financial aid office.

## What if I have documentation that isn t listed above?

You are NOT an eligible noncitizen and cannot receive federal student aid if

- you have only a Notice of Approval to Apply for Permanent Residence (I-171 or I-464),
- you are in the U.S. on an F-1 or F-2 nonimmigrant student visa, or on a J-1 or J-2 nonimmigrant Exchange Visitor Visa, or
- you hold a G series visa (pertaining to international organizations).

## If I m not an eligible noncitizen, can I get any type of financial aid to study in the U.S.?

Yes, there may be some scholarships and other aid you can get.

- Check with your country s embassy or a consulate here in the U.S. or with the appropriate government office back in your country to see what they offer.
- Try the U.S. Department of Labor s free online scholarship search.
- Ask the college or career school you plan to attend whether they offer any aid for students like you.
- Check out the Education USA website.

## Basic Eligibility Criteria

Our basic eligibility requirements are that you must

- demonstrate financial need (for most programs);
- be a U.S. citizen or an eligible noncitizen;
- have a valid Social Security number (with the exception of students from the Republic of the Marshall Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, or the Republic of Palau);
- be registered with Selective Service, if you re a male (you must register between the ages of 18 and 25);
- be enrolled or accepted for enrollment as a regular student in an eligible degree or certificate program;
- be enrolled at least half-time to be eligible for Direct Loan Program funds;
- maintain satisfactory academic progress in college or career school;
- sign the certification statement on the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form stating that
  - you are not in default on a federal student loan,
  - you do not owe money on a federal student grant, and
  - you will use federal student aid only for educational purposes; and
- show you re qualified to obtain a college or career school education by
  - having a high school diploma or a recognized equivalent such as a General Educational Development (GED) certificate;
  - completing a high school education in a homeschool setting approved under state law (or if state law does not require a homeschooled student to obtain a completion credential completing a high school education in a homeschool setting that qualifies as an exemption from compulsory attendance requirements under state law); or
  - enrolling in an eligible career pathway program and meeting one of the "ability-to-benefit" alternatives described below.

Additional eligibility requirements can apply in certain situations including for non-U.S. citizens, students with criminal convictions, and students with intellectual disabilities.

Some federal student aid programs have their own eligibility criteria in addition to the general requirements listed above. Check with your college s financial aid office if you have questions about a particular program.

## Registering for Selective Service

Most male students must be registered with Selective Service to receive federal student aid. You must register if you are a male and are not currently on active duty in the U.S. armed forces. You can call Selective Service toll-free at 1-888-655-1825 for general information about registering, or register online at sss.gov or while completing the FAFSA form.

Note: If you are a citizen of the Federated States of Micronesia, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, or the Republic of Palau, you are exempt from registering.

## Ability-to-Benefit Alternatives

If you were enrolled in college or career school prior to July 1, 2012, or if you are currently enrolled in an eligible career pathway program*, you may show you re qualified to obtain a higher education by

- passing an approved ability-to-benefit test* (if you don t have a diploma or GED, a college can administer a test to determine whether you can benefit from the education offered at that school) or
- completing six credit hours or equivalent course work toward a degree or certificate (you may not receive aid while earning the six credit hours).

# Have you been told you can t get federal student aid any longer?

In most circumstances, there are things you can do to get back your eligibility for financial aid.

You might lose federal student aid eligibility for a number of reasons. For instance, you might no longer meet one of the basic eligibility criteria, or you might have changed majors and no longer be enrolled in a program that makes you eligible to receive a specific type of funding (for instance, a Teacher Education Assistance for College and Higher Education [TEACH] Grant). We recommend you talk to your financial aid office about those and any other circumstances that cause you to lose eligibility.

Meanwhile, below we provide some tips on how to get your eligibility back if you find yourself in one of the following situations:

## What if I defaulted on my student loan but now I want to get more federal student aid?

You ll need to get out of default before you can receive aid again.

## What if my grades slipped, or I haven t completed enough credits, and my financial aid office told me I can t get federal student aid?

You need to make satisfactory academic progress in college or career school in order to keep getting federal student aid. Talk to your school about whether you can appeal the decision that made you ineligible to continue receiving federal student aid.

## What if I was an eligible noncitizen but my status expired or was revoked?

You ll need to reinstate the status that made you an eligible noncitizen, or become a citizen or permanent resident, before you can receive federal student aid. For information about reinstating your status or becoming a citizen, contact U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services.

## What if I was convicted of a drug offense but now I want to get more federal student aid?

If you ve lost eligibility due to a conviction for a drug offense, and you are not scheduled to regain eligibility this academic year, it is possible to regain eligibility early.

## What if I m incarcerated?

Your incarceration affects your eligibility for different types of aid in different ways. If you are ineligible for a particular type of student aid due to your incarceration, you ll need to wait until you re released before you can get that type of aid.

## What if I accidentally received more federal student loan or grant money than I was supposed to?

In certain cases, you ll need to repay the amount that was beyond the maximum that you were allowed to receive. You can either repay the excess all at once, or you can make arrangements to repay it a bit at a time. Once you ve repaid or made arrangements to repay the excess, you ll be able to receive additional federal student aid (assuming you haven t reached the maximum amounts for all programs for which you are otherwise eligible). In other cases, your financial aid office might be able to adjust the amount of money you ll be getting from another federal student aid program to make up for the excess you received. If you have questions about repaying aid or getting additional aid, talk to the financial aid staff at your school.

## What if I thought I had a high school diploma, but it turns out that I actually don t?

This situation might arise if, for instance, your high school is a diploma mill (a school that charges a student a fee and requires him or her to complete little or no course work to get the diploma). If you don t have a high school diploma or an equivalent such as a General Educational Development (GED) certificate, you ll need to talk to the financial aid office at your school to find out what to do.

## What if I was convicted of, or pled nolo contendere or guilty to, a crime involving fraud to obtain federal student aid funds?

You ll need to repay the funds to the U.S. Department of Education or in the case of a federal student loan to the holder or servicer of the loan.

## What if I have property subject to a judgment lien?

If you have property subject to a judgment lien for a debt owed to the United States, you will have to pay your debt in full or make arrangements to pay the debt."}, {"chunk_id": "Reporting Parent Information | Federal Student Aid#1_0::c0007", "text": "[受抚养学生必须在其联邦学生援助免费申请（FAFSA）表格上报告其家长信息以及自己的信息。 > 如果我因特殊情况无法提供父母信息怎么办？]

## VA预约工具如何帮助我管理我的医疗保健？

VA预约工具提供了一种安全的、基于网络的方式，用于在线安排、查看和组织您的VA预约。

您可以使用这些工具来：

- 在线安排部分VA医疗预约
- 重新安排和取消在线进行的预约
- 在您的健康日历上查看预约
- 查找您预约的VA设施的位置
- 为即将到来的预约设置电子邮件提醒
- 打印您未来预约的列表
- 查找过去2年的历史预约
- 将非VA预约添加到您的健康日历

## 我是否有资格使用VA预约工具？

如果您满足以下列出的所有要求，您可以使用这些工具。

以下所有条件都必须满足。您：

- 已注册VA健康护理，并且
- 正在预约使用在线预约的VA健康机构，并且
- 在过去2年内曾在该VA健康机构有过预约

了解如何申请VA健康护理

并且，您必须拥有以下免费账户之一：

- 一个Premium My HealtheVet账户，或
- 一个Premium DS Logon账户（用于eBenefits和milConnect），或
- 一个已验证的ID.me账户，您可以在VA.gov上创建

了解3种不同的My HealtheVet账户类型

您可以查看我们目前使用在线预约工具的VA机构列表。我们希望未来能扩大VA机构和预约类型的数量。

查看目前使用在线预约的VA机构列表

## 我可以在线预约哪些类型的VA医疗预约？

这取决于您接受护理的VA健康机构。

您或许可以预约以下门诊预约：

- 初级护理
- 心理健康
- 验光
- 听力

请与您接受护理的具体机构核实，询问在线预约事宜。查看目前使用在线预约的VA机构查找VA健康机构

## 我可以使用此工具预约非VA预约吗？

不可以。了解更多关于从非VA提供者获得护理的信息。

## 我可以通过VA安全消息安排预约吗？

如果您与VA医疗团队使用Secure Messaging，您或许可以通过此服务来安排和取消预约。了解更多关于Secure Messaging的信息

## 我的个人健康信息会受到保护吗？

是的。这是一个安全的网站。我们遵循严格的安全政策和实践来保护您的个人健康信息。并且只有您和您的VA医疗团队能够访问您的安全消息。

如果您打印或下载任何消息，您需要负责保护这些信息。获取保护个人健康信息的提示

## VA预约工具如何帮助我管理我的医疗保健？

VA预约工具提供了一种安全的、基于网络的方式，用于在线安排、查看和组织您的VA预约。

您可以使用这些工具来：

- 在线安排部分VA医疗预约
- 重新安排和取消在线进行的预约
- 在您的健康日历上查看预约
- 查找您预约的VA设施的位置
- 为即将到来的预约设置电子邮件提醒
- 打印您未来预约的列表
- 查找过去2年的历史预约
- 将非VA预约添加到您的健康日历

## 我是否有资格使用VA预约工具？

如果您满足以下列出的所有要求，您可以使用这些工具。

以下所有条件都必须满足。您：

- 已注册VA健康护理，并且
- 正在预约使用在线预约的VA健康机构，并且
- 在过去2年内曾在该VA健康机构有过预约

了解如何申请VA健康护理

并且，您必须拥有以下免费账户之一：

- 一个Premium My HealtheVet账户，或
- 一个Premium DS Logon账户（用于eBenefits和milConnect），或
- 一个已验证的ID.me账户，您可以在VA.gov上创建

了解3种不同的My HealtheVet账户类型

# 尽可能多地寻找和申请奖学金——这是上大学或职业学校的免费资金！

尽早开始研究，并按时提交申请，你可能会在奖学金申请上取得成功。

奖学金是赠款，无需偿还。有数千种奖学金，由学校、雇主、个人、私营公司、非营利组织、社区、宗教团体以及专业和社会组织提供。

## 有哪些类型的奖学金？

一些大学奖学金是基于成绩的。你通过达到或超过奖学金提供者设定的某些标准来获得它们。成绩奖学金可能基于学业成就或学业与特殊才能、特质或兴趣的结合来授予。其他奖学金则基于经济需求。

许多奖学金面向特定人群；例如，有面向女性或研究生的奖学金。还有一些奖学金是因为你或你父母的工作地点，或者因为你来自某个特定背景（例如，有面向军人家庭的奖学金）。

奖学金可能覆盖你的全部学费，也可能是一次性几百美元的奖励。无论如何，都值得申请，因为它将有助于降低你的教育成本。

## 如何找到奖学金？

你可以通过多种方式了解奖学金，包括联系你计划就读学校的财务援助办公室，以及在公共图书馆或网上查看信息。但要小心。确保你收到的奖学金信息和录取通知是合法的；并记住，你不必付费就能找到奖学金或其他财务援助。查看我们关于如何避免诈骗的信息。

尝试这些免费的奖学金信息来源：

- 大学或职业学校的财务援助办公室
- 高中或TRIO顾问
- 美国劳工部的免费奖学金搜索工具
-
- 你所在州的助学金机构
- 你图书馆的参考书区
- 基金会、宗教或社区组织、当地企业或公民团体
- 与你兴趣领域相关的组织（包括专业协会）
- 基于族裔的组织
- 你的雇主或你父母的雇主

## 我什么时候申请奖学金？

这取决于每个奖学金的截止日期。有些截止日期早在大学开学前一年，所以如果你现在在读高中，你应该在高二和高三之间的暑假研究和申请奖学金。但如果你错过了那个时间窗口，不要放弃！查看奖学金信息，看看现在还有哪些你可以申请。

## 我如何申请奖学金？

每个奖学金都有自己的要求。奖学金的网站应该会告诉你谁有资格获得该奖学金以及如何申请。确保你仔细阅读申请表，完整填写，并在申请截止日期前提交。

## 我如何获得奖学金资金？

这取决于奖学金。资金可能直接支付给你的大学，用于支付你欠下的任何学费、杂费或其他金额，然后剩余的资金会给你。或者可能以支票形式直接寄给你。奖学金提供者在通知你获得奖学金时，应该会告诉你预期情况。如果没有，一定要询问。

## 奖学金如何影响我的其他学生资助？

奖学金会影响你的其他学生资助，因为你所有学生资助加起来不能超过你在大学或职业学校的出勤成本。因此，如果你获得了奖学金，你需要告知你的学校，以便经济援助办公室从你的出勤成本（以及你可能获得的其他某些援助，如贷款）中减去该金额。然后，剩余的任何金额可以由你有资格获得的其他经济援助来覆盖。有问题吗？请咨询你的经济援助办公室。"}, {"chunk_id": "Loan Servicers | Federal Student Aid#1_0::c0003", "text": "[谁是我的学生贷款服务商？ > 贷款信息联系谁]

# Accepting Financial Aid

First, accept the financial aid funds you don t have to pay back.

When your school financial aid office sends you an aid offer, they ll ask you to indicate which financial aid you want. Look carefully at your options and make an informed decision.

## Choosing the Best Financial Aid to Accept

Keep the following in mind when you get an aid offer and are deciding which aid is the best to accept:

- Free money first (e.g., scholarships, grants)
- Earned money second (e.g., work-study)
- Borrowed money last (e.g., federal student loans)

Start from the top of this table and work your way down:

Many schools also offer tuition payment plans (a monthly interest-free payment toward tuition). This type of plan may help reduce the amount you need to take out in loans. Ask your financial aid office if such a plan is available.

## Deciding Which Student Loans to Accept

If you must accept loans, accept the ones with the most favorable terms and conditions. Usually, that means choosing the federal student loans offered to you. If you are considering getting a state loan, school loan, or private student loan, you should learn about the differences between federal and other loans.

If you have any questions or don t understand what types of loans are in your aid offer, contact the school. Make sure you understand what you re accepting and the repayment terms.

Borrow only what you need! If your living expenses are not going to be as high as the amount estimated by your school, you have the right to turn down the loan or to request a lower loan amount. In the aid offer, your school will tell you how to do this.

To determine how much loan money to accept, make a list of your college and living expenses and the resources you ll have available to pay them; in other words, make a budget to help ensure you borrow only what you need.

Remember: If you don t accept the full amount of the loan you re eligible for, you can increase the amount later.

## Informing Your School About Aid You ll Accept

Your student aid offer will include directions on accepting aid. Follow those directions carefully. You might have to enter the amounts you re accepting in an online form and then submit the form. If you receive a paper aid offer, you might have to sign it and mail it back to the school.

Accepting a loan or grant listed in the aid offer may involve additional steps, which vary depending on the type of loan or grant you re receiving. Saying yes may be as simple as signing a promissory note a contract between you and the lender* that specifies the terms and conditions of the loan or it may include entrance counseling if this is your first federal loan.

By signing the promissory note, you are promising to repay your student loan. The financial aid office will guide you through the paperwork or direct you to the online *Master Promissory Note* if appropriate.

## 有哪些类型的奖学金？

一些大学奖学金是基于成绩的。你通过达到或超过奖学金提供者设定的某些标准来获得它们。成绩奖学金可能基于学业成就或学业与特殊才能、特质或兴趣的结合来授予。其他奖学金则基于经济需求。

## Benefits Planner: Retirement

### Benefits For Your Spouse

Even if you have never worked under Social Security, you may be able to get spouse s retirement benefits if you are at least 62 years of age and your spouse is receiving retirement or disability benefits. You can also qualify for Medicare at age 65.

If you are divorced, you may still be able to get benefits on your ex-spouse's record. For information on the requirements for Divorced Spouse's Benefits, read "If You Are Divorced

You can receive the spouse's benefit no matter what your age is if you are caring for their child who is also receiving benefits.

### How Much Will I Receive?

If you qualify and apply for your own retirement benefits and for benefits as a spouse, we always pay your own benefits first. If your benefits as a spouse are higher than your own retirement benefits, you will get a combination of benefits equaling the higher spouse benefit.

Your benefits as a spouse do not include any delayed retirement credits your spouse may receive.

If you begin receiving benefits:

- between age 62 and your full retirement age, the amount will be permanently reduced by a percentage based on the number of months up to your full retirement age.

 

- If you are under full retirement age and you continue to work while receiving benefits, your benefits may be affected by the retirement earnings test.

- at your full retirement age, your benefit as a spouse cannot exceed one-half of your spouse's full retirement amount.

 

- If you were born before January 2, 1954 and have already reached full retirement age, you can choose to receive only the spouse s benefit and delay receiving your retirement benefit until a later date. If your spouse is full retirement age and applying for spouse s benefits only, they can apply online by using the retirement application. Your spouse can also contact us to schedule an appointment.

If your spouse s birthday is January 2, 1954 or later, the option to take only one benefit at full retirement age no longer exists. If your spouse files for one benefit, they will be effectively filing for all retirement or spousal benefits.

If you will receive a pension for work not covered by Social Security such as government employment, the amount of your Social Security benefits on your spouse's record may be reduced.

Benefits paid to you as a spouse will not decrease your spouse s retirement benefit. In fact, the value of the benefits you may receive, added to their benefits, may help your spouse decide if taking benefits sooner may be more advantageous.

#### Maximum Family Benefits

If one of your spouse's children also qualifies for benefits, there is a limit to the amount we can pay family members.

The total depends on your spouse's benefit amount and the number of family members who also qualify on the same record. The total varies, but generally the total amount the worker (your spouse) and their family members can receive is about 150 to 180 percent of the worker's full retirement benefit.

If there is an ex-spouse who also qualifies for benefits, they will not affect the total amount of benefits you or your family may receive.

### How Do I Apply?

You can apply:

- Online - Use our Social Security Retirement/Medicare Benefit Application to apply for retirement, spouse's, divorced spouse's or Medicare benefits.

 

- If your spouse is already receiving benefits when you apply, or if you and your spouse apply at the same time, we will also check your eligibility for benefits as a spouse. If you qualify, your application will automatically serve as a request for spousal benefits.

- By phone - Call us at 1-800-772-1213. If you are deaf or hard of hearing, you can call us at TTY 1-800-325-0778.

 

- In person - Visit your local Social Security office. (Call first to make an appointment.)

- If you do not live in the U.S. or one of its territories you can also - Contact the nearest U.S. Social Security office, U.S. Embassy or consulate.

### Next Steps

## 符合条件的联邦贷款

以下来自威廉·D·福特联邦直接贷款（直接贷款）计划和联邦家庭教育贷款（FFEL）计划的贷款符合扩展还款计划的条件：

## 扩展还款计划的资格

如果您是直接贷款借款人，您必须在1998年10月7日或之后获得直接贷款之日没有未偿还的直接贷款余额，并且您必须拥有超过30,000美元的未偿还直接贷款。

如果您是FFEL借款人，要符合此计划的条件，您必须在1998年10月7日或之后获得FFEL计划贷款之日没有未偿还的FFEL计划贷款余额，并且您必须拥有超过30,000美元的未偿还FFEL计划贷款。

例如，如果您有35,000美元的未偿还FFEL计划贷款和10,000美元的未偿还直接贷款，您可以为您的FFEL计划贷款选择扩展还款计划，但不能为您的直接贷款选择。

- 固定或递增的金额，
- 最长还款期限为25年，并且
- 通常低于标准还款计划和递增还款计划下的还款额。

## 使用贷款模拟器估算您在扩展还款计划下的资格和还款金额

您的贷款服务机构，即处理您的联邦学生贷款账单和其他服务的公司，可以帮助您选择最适合您的贷款还款计划。在联系您的贷款服务机构讨论还款计划之前，您可以使用我们的贷款模拟器提前了解您可能符合条件的计划，并获得所有联邦学生贷款还款计划的预计月还款额比较。此比较很重要，因为扩展计划可能不会根据您的个人情况提供最低的还款金额。您可能会发现，在另一个还款计划下，您的还款额会更低。"}, {"chunk_id": "Standard Plan | Federal Student Aid#1_0::c0000", "text": "# 标准还款计划 | 联邦学生援助

# 标准还款计划是威廉·D·福特联邦直接贷款（直接贷款）计划和联邦家庭教育贷款（FFEL）计划下贷款的基本还款计划。

还款金额固定，最长还款期为10年（合并贷款为10至30年）。

该还款计划从长远来看能为您节省资金，因为您的每月还款额可能略高于其他计划下的还款额，但您将在最短时间内还清贷款。因此，在整个贷款期限内，您支付的利息总额将是最少的。

当需要偿还贷款时，您可以选择还款计划。如果您未选择其他还款计划，您的贷款服务机构（负责处理您的联邦教育贷款账单及其他服务的公司）将为您安排标准还款计划。

## 符合条件的联邦贷款

以下来自直接贷款计划和FFEL计划的贷款符合标准还款计划的条件：

- 直接补贴贷款
- 直接非补贴贷款
- 直接PLUS贷款
- 直接合并贷款
- 补贴联邦斯塔福德贷款
- 非补贴联邦斯塔福德贷款
- FFEL PLUS贷款

 

- FFEL合并贷款

请注意，自2010年7月1日起，FFEL计划下不再发放新贷款。

## 联邦教育贷款（合并贷款除外）的每月还款额

在此计划下，您的每月还款额为固定金额，每月至少50美元，最长还款期为10年，适用于除直接合并贷款和FFEL合并贷款以外的所有贷款类型。

## 合并贷款的每月还款额

在此计划下，您的每月还款额为

- 每月固定金额至少50美元，并且

当您在延期偿还期间负责支付贷款利息时，您可以选择在利息产生时支付，或者允许其累积并在延期偿还期结束时资本化（添加到您的贷款本金余额中）。如果您不支付贷款利息并允许其资本化，您在贷款期限内偿还的总金额可能会更高。未付利息仅在直接贷款和联邦家庭教育贷款计划贷款上资本化。珀金斯贷款上的未付利息永远不会资本化。"}, {"chunk_id": "Student Loan Deferment | Federal Student Aid#1_0::c0003", "text": "[学生贷款延期偿还允许您暂时停止还款。 > 了解延期偿还的资格]
有多种情况可能使您有资格获得联邦学生贷款的延期偿还。

### 癌症治疗延期偿还

在接受癌症治疗期间以及治疗结束后的六个月内，您可能有资格获得此延期偿还。

填写*癌症治疗延期偿还申请表*。

### 经济困难延期还款

如果您符合以下条件，您可能有资格获得此延期还款：

- 正在领取基于经济状况调查的福利，如公共援助（例如，贫困家庭临时援助（TANF））；
- 全职工作但收入低于您家庭规模和居住州贫困指南的150%；或
- 正在和平队服役。

您最多只能获得此延期还款三年。

填写经济困难延期还款申请表。

### 研究生奖学金延期还款

如果您被录取到经批准的研究生奖学金项目，您可能有资格获得此延期还款。研究生奖学金项目通常是为研究生提供经济支持以进行研究生学习和研究的项目。大多数研究生奖学金项目面向博士生，但有些也面向硕士生。

填写研究生奖学金延期还款申请表。

### 在校延期还款

如果您在符合条件的学院或职业学校至少半日制注册，您就有资格获得此延期还款。如果您是获得直接PLUS贷款的研究生或专业学生，您在停止至少半日制注册后，有资格获得额外六个月的延期还款。

重要！如果您在符合条件的学院或职业学校至少半日制注册，在大多数情况下，您的贷款将根据您学校报告的注册信息自动进入延期还款状态，您的贷款服务机构将通知您延期还款已获批准。如果您至少半日制注册但没有自动获得延期还款，您应联系您注册的学校。您的学校随后将报告有关您注册状态的信息，以便您的贷款可以进入延期还款状态。

填写在校延期还款申请表。

注意：在校延期还款通常是自动的，因此在大多数情况下无需填写在校延期还款申请表。但是，如果您至少半日制注册但没有自动获得延期还款，您可以按照上述说明要求您的学校报告您的注册信息，或填写在校延期还款申请表。

### 兵役和现役后学生延期还款

如果您符合以下条件，您可能有资格获得此延期还款：

- 您正在与战争、军事行动或国家紧急状态相关的现役军事服役中；或
- 您已完成符合条件的现役服役以及任何适用的宽限期。此延期还款在您以至少半日制身份重新注册到符合条件的学院或职业学校时结束，或在现役服役完成日期及任何适用宽限期后13个月结束，以较早者为准。

填写*兵役和现役后学生延期还款申请表*。

### 家长PLUS借款人延期还款

如果您是家长，为了帮助支付孩子的教育费用而获得了Direct PLUS贷款，并且您为其贷款的学生至少在半日制就读于符合条件的学院或职业学校，则您可能有资格获得此延期。在学生不再至少半日制就读后，您还可以额外获得六个月的延期。

填写*家长PLUS借款人延期申请表*。

注意：作为填写家长PLUS借款人延期申请表的替代方案，如果您孩子就读的学校要求您填写Direct PLUS贷款申请表，您可以在提交Direct PLUS贷款申请表时请求此延期。请咨询您孩子所在的学校。

### 康复培训延期

如果您参加了一个经批准的康复培训项目，该项目旨在提供职业、药物滥用、心理健康或酒精滥用康复治疗，则您可能有资格获得此延期。

填写*康复培训延期申请表*。

### 失业延期

如果您领取失业救济金，或者您正在寻找全职工作但未能找到，则您可能有资格获得此延期。您最多可以获得三年的此延期。

填写失业延期申请表。

# 扩展还款计划允许您在较长时间内偿还贷款。

还款期限最长可达25年。

如果您需要在比标准还款计划等计划更长的时间内支付较低的月供，那么扩展还款计划可能适合您。

## 符合条件的联邦贷款

以下来自威廉·D·福特联邦直接贷款（直接贷款）计划和联邦家庭教育贷款（FFEL）计划的贷款符合扩展还款计划的条件：

- 直接补贴贷款
- 直接无补贴贷款
- 直接PLUS贷款
- 直接合并贷款
- 补贴联邦斯塔福德贷款
- 无补贴联邦斯塔福德贷款
- FFEL PLUS贷款
- FFEL合并贷款

## 扩展还款计划的资格

如果您是直接贷款借款人，您必须在1998年10月7日或之后获得直接贷款之日没有未偿还的直接贷款余额，并且您必须拥有超过30,000美元的未偿还直接贷款。

如果您是FFEL借款人，要符合此计划的条件，您必须在1998年10月7日或之后获得FFEL计划贷款之日没有未偿还的FFEL计划贷款余额，并且您必须拥有超过30,000美元的未偿还FFEL计划贷款。

例如，如果您有35,000美元的未偿还FFEL计划贷款和10,000美元的未偿还直接贷款，您可以为您的FFEL计划贷款选择扩展还款计划，但不能为您的直接贷款选择。

## 每月还款额

在此计划下，您的每月还款额为

- 固定或递增的金额，
- 最长还款期限为25年，并且
- 通常低于标准还款计划和递增还款计划下的还款额。

## 使用贷款模拟器估算您在扩展还款计划下的资格和还款金额

您的贷款服务机构，即处理您的联邦学生贷款账单和其他服务的公司，可以帮助您选择最适合您的贷款还款计划。在联系您的贷款服务机构讨论还款计划之前，您可以使用我们的贷款模拟器提前了解您可能符合条件的计划，并获得所有联邦学生贷款还款计划的预计月还款额比较。此比较很重要，因为扩展计划可能不会根据您的个人情况提供最低的还款金额。您可能会发现，在另一个还款计划下，您的还款额会更低。"}, {"chunk_id": "Student Loan Deferment | Federal Student Aid#1_0::c0004", "text": "[学生贷款延期偿还允许您暂时停止还款。 > 符合延期条件的贷款类型]

在大多数情况下，获得延期的珀金斯贷款借款人将获得六个月的延期后宽限期，该宽限期从他们不再满足延期资格要求之日起开始。在延期后宽限期内无需还款。

- 您要合并的贷款必须处于还款期或宽限期。

# 标准还款计划是威廉·D·福特联邦直接贷款（直接贷款）计划和联邦家庭教育贷款（FFEL）计划下贷款的基本还款计划。

还款金额固定，最长还款期为10年（合并贷款为10至30年）。

该还款计划从长远来看能为您节省资金，因为您的每月还款额可能略高于其他计划下的还款额，但您将在最短时间内还清贷款。因此，在整个贷款期限内，您支付的利息总额将是最少的。

当需要偿还贷款时，您可以选择还款计划。如果您未选择其他还款计划，您的贷款服务机构（负责处理您的联邦教育贷款账单及其他服务的公司）将为您安排标准还款计划。

## 符合条件的联邦贷款

以下来自直接贷款计划和FFEL计划的贷款符合标准还款计划的条件：

- 直接补贴贷款
- 直接非补贴贷款
- 直接PLUS贷款
- 直接合并贷款
- 补贴联邦斯塔福德贷款
- 非补贴联邦斯塔福德贷款
- FFEL PLUS贷款

 

- FFEL合并贷款

请注意，自2010年7月1日起，FFEL计划下不再发放新贷款。

## 联邦教育贷款（合并贷款除外）的每月还款额

在此计划下，您的每月还款额为固定金额，每月至少50美元，最长还款期为10年，适用于除直接合并贷款和FFEL合并贷款以外的所有贷款类型。

## 合并贷款的每月还款额

在此计划下，您的每月还款额为

- 每月固定金额至少50美元，并且
- 直接合并贷款和FFEL合并贷款的还款期为10至30年。

如果您有直接合并贷款或FFEL合并贷款，您的还款期长度将取决于您的总教育贷款债务金额。此总教育贷款债务包括您的合并贷款金额和其他学生贷款债务。其他学生贷款债务包括未纳入合并贷款的任何联邦学生贷款，以及不符合合并条件的私人教育贷款。

在确定您的还款期时，可考虑的其他学生贷款债务的最高金额不得超过您正在合并的贷款金额。

要将其他学生贷款债务纳入直接合并贷款还款期的确定中，请务必在合并申请中列出这些贷款，在用于列出您不希望合并但希望纳入还款期确定范围的贷款的栏目中填写。

有多种情况可能使您有资格获得联邦学生贷款的延期偿还。

### 癌症治疗延期偿还

在接受癌症治疗期间以及治疗结束后的六个月内，您可能有资格获得此延期偿还。

- 通常低于标准还款计划和递增还款计划下的还款额。

## Multiple party or contested claims

If you re one of multiple people claiming the right to the same benefit, you have 60 days to appeal to a Veterans Law Judge at the Board of Veterans Appeals in Washington, D.C. A judge who s an expert in Veterans law will review your case.

## Mark your calendar

You have 60 days from the date on your decision to request a Board Appeal.

## Can I add new evidence?

You have the option to add new evidence for a judge to review. You ll have to submit this evidence within 90 days from the date VA receives your Board Appeal form.

This option will take longer.

## Can I request a hearing?

You have the option to request a hearing with a judge. A video conference hearing will take place at a VA location near you.

This option will take longer.

## What happens at a hearing?

You and the judge will have a conversation. The judge will listen to your testimony. The judge may ask you a few questions. Your representative, if you have one, may help you at the hearing.

The hearing will be transcribed and added to your appeal file. You can add new and relevant evidence within 90 days after the hearing, but it isn t required.

## How do I request a Board Appeal?

To request a Board Appeal, fill out the Decision Review Request: Board Appeal (VA Form 10182). Download VA Form 10182 (PDF)

### Choose one of the 3 options to appeal with a Veterans Law Judge

Direct Review If you want a Veterans Law Judge to review your case as quickly as possible, choose a Direct Review.

You can t submit any evidence.

About 1 year The Board s goal for deciding appeals with no new evidence and no hearing is about a year.

Evidence Submission If you have additional evidence for a Veterans Law Judge to review, choose Evidence Submission.

You must submit evidence within 90 days of the date VA receives your Board Appeal form.

Longer If you add new evidence, it ll take longer than the Direct Review appeal option.

Hearing Request If you want a video conference hearing with a Veterans Law Judge at a nearby VA location, choose a Hearing Request.

At your hearing, you and a Veterans Law Judge will have a conversation, and they ll ask you questions about your appeal. Your hearing will be transcribed and added to your appeal file. Learn more about hearings and how to request one

You can add new and relevant evidence within 90 days after the hearing, but it isn t required.

Longer If you request a hearing, it ll take longer than the Direct Review appeal option.

### List the issue(s) you want to appeal in Part III

You can include all or just some of the issues VA has decided. You ll need to list the issue(s) you disagree with and the VA decision date for each.

## Multiple party or contested claims

If you re one of multiple people claiming the right to the same benefit, you have 60 days to appeal to a Veterans Law Judge at the Board of Veterans Appeals in Washington, D.C. A judge who s an expert in Veterans law will review your case.

## Mark your calendar

You have 60 days from the date on your decision to request a Board Appeal.

## Can I add new evidence?

You have the option to add new evidence for a judge to review. You ll have to submit this evidence within 90 days from the date VA receives your Board Appeal form.

This option will take longer.

## Can I request a hearing?

You have the option to request a hearing with a judge. A video conference hearing will take place at a VA location near you.

This option will take longer.

## What happens at a hearing?

You and the judge will have a conversation. The judge will listen to your testimony. The judge may ask you a few questions. Your representative, if you have one, may help you at the hearing.

The hearing will be transcribed and added to your appeal file. You can add new and relevant evidence within 90 days after the hearing, but it isn t required.

## How do I request a Board Appeal?

To request a Board Appeal, fill out the Decision Review Request: Board Appeal (VA Form 10182). Download VA Form 10182 (PDF)

### Choose one of the 3 options to appeal with a Veterans Law Judge

Direct Review If you want a Veterans Law Judge to review your case as quickly as possible, choose a Direct Review.

You can t submit any evidence.

About 1 year The Board s goal for deciding appeals with no new evidence and no hearing is about a year.

Evidence Submission If you have additional evidence for a Veterans Law Judge to review, choose Evidence Submission.

You must submit evidence within 90 days of the date VA receives your Board Appeal form.

Longer If you add new evidence, it ll take longer than the Direct Review appeal option.

Hearing Request If you want a video conference hearing with a Veterans Law Judge at a nearby VA location, choose a Hearing Request.

At your hearing, you and a Veterans Law Judge will have a conversation, and they ll ask you questions about your appeal. Your hearing will be transcribed and added to your appeal file. Learn more about hearings and how to request one

You can add new and relevant evidence within 90 days after the hearing, but it isn t required.

Longer If you request a hearing, it ll take longer than the Direct Review appeal option.

### List the issue(s) you want to appeal in Part III

You can include all or just some of the issues VA has decided. You ll need to list the issue(s) you disagree with and the VA decision date for each.

# VA 决策复核与上诉

如果您不同意 VA 的决策，您可以选择以下复核选项之一来继续您的案件。如果您对该复核结果不满意，您可以尝试另一个选项。

#### 标记您的日历

您有自决策日期起 1 年的时间来请求决策复核，除非您有 fiduciary claim 或 multiple party claim。请查看这些罕见情况是否适用于您

## 决策复核选项

- 添加新的且相关的证据（提交 Supplemental Claim）
- 请求高级审阅员重新审查（请求 Higher-Level Review）
- 向 Veterans Law Judge 上诉（请求 Board Appeal）

### 添加新的且相关的证据

下载 VA Form 20-0995：Supplemental Claim（PDF）

当您选择提交 Supplemental Claim 时，您是在添加支持您案件的新证据或指明需要审查的证据。审阅员将查看所有证据并确定是否改变决策。了解如何提交 Supplemental Claim

您必须提交 VA 之前没有的、支持您案件的证据。

4-5 个月 VA 完成 Supplemental Claims 的目标是 125 天。

#### 我可以提交 Supplemental Claim 吗？

如果您有新证据，您可以在决策后 1 年内提交 Supplemental Claim。

但如果您有 fiduciary claim 或您是多个声称同一福利的人之一（这种情况很少见），则不能提交 Supplemental Claim。请查看这些罕见情况是否适用于您

### 请求高级审阅员重新审查

下载 VA Form 20-0996：Higher-Level Review（PDF）

当您选择请求 Higher-Level Review 时，您是在请求对相同证据进行另一次审查。高级审阅员将重新审查您的案件，并确定是否可以根据意见分歧或 VA 犯下的错误来更改决策。了解如何请求 Higher-Level Review

您无法提交任何证据。

您和/或您的代表可以通过电话与审核员沟通。您可以告诉他们为什么您认为决定应被更改，并指出错误。

4-5个月 VA完成Higher-Level Reviews的目标是125天。如果VA需要获取记录或安排新的考试以纠正错误，审核可能需要更长时间。

#### 我可以申请Higher-Level Review吗？

您可以对初始申请或Supplemental Claim决定申请Higher-Level Review。在Higher-Level Review或Board Appeal之后，此选项不可用。

### 向Veterans Law Judge上诉

下载VA Form 10182: Board Appeal (PDF)

位于华盛顿特区的Board of Veterans Appeals的法官将审核您的案件。了解更多关于如何申请Board Appeal的信息

约1年 Board对无新证据且无听证的上诉作出决定的目标时间约为一年。

您可以选择添加法官将审核的新证据。

您也可以选择请求与法官进行听证，可以在华盛顿特区亲自进行，或通过视频会议在您附近的VA地点进行。

更长 如果您提交新证据或请求听证，Board将需要更长时间来决定您的上诉。

#### 我可以申请Board Appeal吗？

您可以在初始申请、Supplemental Claim或Higher-Level Review决定后申请Board Appeal。您不能连续两次申请Board Appeal。

## Board决定之后

如果您不同意Board的决定，并且有支持您案件的新且相关的证据，您可以提交Supplemental Claim。您也可以向U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims提出上诉。了解更多关于Board决定后您的选择

# VA 决策复核与上诉

如果您不同意 VA 的决策，您可以选择以下复核选项之一来继续您的案件。如果您对该复核结果不满意，您可以尝试另一个选项。

#### 标记您的日历

您有自决策日期起 1 年的时间来请求决策复核，除非您有 fiduciary claim 或 multiple party claim。请查看这些罕见情况是否适用于您

## 决策复核选项

- 添加新的且相关的证据（提交 Supplemental Claim）
- 请求高级审阅员重新审查（请求 Higher-Level Review）
- 向 Veterans Law Judge 上诉（请求 Board Appeal）

### 添加新的且相关的证据

下载 VA Form 20-0995：Supplemental Claim（PDF）

当您选择提交 Supplemental Claim 时，您是在添加支持您案件的新证据或指明需要审查的证据。审阅员将查看所有证据并确定是否改变决策。了解如何提交 Supplemental Claim

您必须提交 VA 之前没有的、支持您案件的证据。

4-5 个月 VA 完成 Supplemental Claims 的目标是 125 天。

#### 我可以提交 Supplemental Claim 吗？

如果您有新证据，您可以在决策后 1 年内提交 Supplemental Claim。

但如果您有 fiduciary claim 或您是多个声称同一福利的人之一（这种情况很少见），则不能提交 Supplemental Claim。请查看这些罕见情况是否适用于您

### 请求高级审阅员重新审查

下载 VA Form 20-0996：Higher-Level Review（PDF）

当您选择请求 Higher-Level Review 时，您是在请求对相同证据进行另一次审查。高级审阅员将重新审查您的案件，并确定是否可以根据意见分歧或 VA 犯下的错误来更改决策。了解如何请求 Higher-Level Review

您无法提交任何证据。

您和/或您的代表可以通过电话与审核员沟通。您可以告诉他们为什么您认为决定应被更改，并指出错误。

4-5个月 VA完成Higher-Level Reviews的目标是125天。如果VA需要获取记录或安排新的考试以纠正错误，审核可能需要更长时间。

#### 我可以申请Higher-Level Review吗？

您可以对初始申请或Supplemental Claim决定申请Higher-Level Review。在Higher-Level Review或Board Appeal之后，此选项不可用。

### 向Veterans Law Judge上诉

下载VA Form 10182: Board Appeal (PDF)

位于华盛顿特区的Board of Veterans Appeals的法官将审核您的案件。了解更多关于如何申请Board Appeal的信息

约1年 Board对无新证据且无听证的上诉作出决定的目标时间约为一年。

您可以选择添加法官将审核的新证据。

您也可以选择请求与法官进行听证，可以在华盛顿特区亲自进行，或通过视频会议在您附近的VA地点进行。

更长 如果您提交新证据或请求听证，Board将需要更长时间来决定您的上诉。

#### 我可以申请Board Appeal吗？

您可以在初始申请、Supplemental Claim或Higher-Level Review决定后申请Board Appeal。您不能连续两次申请Board Appeal。

## Board决定之后

如果您不同意Board的决定，并且有支持您案件的新且相关的证据，您可以提交Supplemental Claim。您也可以向U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims提出上诉。了解更多关于Board决定后您的选择

跟踪您的索赔或上诉状态

If you were recently denied Social Security benefits or Supplemental Security Income (SSI), you may request an appeal. Generally, you have 60 days after you receive the notice of our decision to ask for any type of appeal. There are four levels of appeal:

- Reconsideration,
- Hearing by an administrative law judge,
- Review by the Appeals Council, and
- Federal Court review (Please see the bottom of page for information on the Federal Court Review Process).

You can request an appeal online for a reconsideration, a hearing by an administrative law judge, and a review by the Appeals Council, even if you live outside of the United States. When we made the first determination on your claim, we sent you a letter explaining our determination. This letter contains guidance on what level of appeal you should select.

To learn more about each appeal level, visit Information About Social Security's Hearings and Appeals Process.

Reconsideration

### Request a Reconsideration Online for a Medical Determination

If your disability claim was recently denied for medical reasons, you can request an appeal online.

A reconsideration is a complete review of your claim by someone who did not take part in the first determination. We will look at all the evidence submitted used in the original determination, plus any new evidence.

Request Medical Reconsideration Continue Request for Medical Reconsideration You Started

### Request a Reconsideration Online for a Non-Medical Determination

If you received a non-medical determination letter from us that you disagree with or you were denied for a reason that is not disability related (for example: income, resources, overpayments, living arrangements), you can request a non-medical appeal online.

Request Non-Medical Reconsideration

### Check the Status of Your Reconsideration

Whether you applied online, by phone, or in an office, you can check the status of your disability and SSI Reconsideration using your personal my Social Security account. ### Request a Hearing for a Medical Determination Online

A hearing is conducted by an administrative law judge who had no part in the original determination or the reconsideration of your case. The hearing is usually held within 75 miles of your home. If you disagree with the determination we made at the reconsideration level, you may request a hearing online.

Request Medical Hearing Continue Medical Hearing Request You Started

Request Non-Medical Hearing

Sign In or Create Account

Request for Review by the Appeals Council

### Request an Appeals Council review of a decision or dismissal made by an administrative law judge

The Appeals Council looks at all requests for review, but it may deny a request if it believes the hearing decision was supported and in accordance with social security law and regulations. If the Appeals Council decides to review your case, it will either decide your case itself or return it to an administrative law judge for further review. If you disagree with the hearing decision, you may request a review by Social Security s Appeals Council online.

Request Appeals Council Review

Federal Court review

If you disagree with the Appeals Council's decision, or if the Appeals Council decides not to review your case, you can file a civil suit in a federal district court. This is the last level of the appeals process. Currently, this process is not available online. To learn more about this process, visit Federal Court Review Process.

## Benefits Planner: Disability \| How You Apply

You should apply for disability benefits as soon as you become disabled. If you are ready to apply now, you can:

- Complete your application online.
- Call our toll-free telephone number **1-800-772-1213**. If you are deaf or hard of hearing, you can call us at TTY **1-800-325-0778**.
- Call or visit your local Social Security office.

If you want to apply in person, please call and make an appointment **before** you visit your local office.

If you wish to help another person apply for disability benefits, please read .

### Information You Need To Apply

Here is the kind of information you should have:

### Information About You

- Your Social Security number and proof of your age;
- Names, addresses, and phone numbers of doctors, caseworkers, hospitals, and clinics that took care of you and the dates of your visits;
- Names and dosages of all the medications you are taking;
- Medical records from your doctors, therapists, hospitals, clinics, and caseworkers, that you already have in your possession;
- Laboratory and test results;
- A summary of where you worked and the kind of work you did; and
- Your most recent W-2 form or, if you were self-employed, a copy of your federal tax return.

### Information About Family Members

- Social Security numbers and proof of age for each family member who may qualify for benefits; and
- Proof of marriage, if your spouse is applying for benefits, as well as dates of prior marriages, if applicable.

The documents you may need to show us must be original documents or copies certified by the issuing office. You can mail or bring them to Social Security. We will make photocopies and return your original documents.

If you don't have all the documents you need, don't delay filing for benefits. We will help you get the information you need.

### More Help For Filing Your Claim

Our Disability Starter Kit will help you get ready for your disability interview or online application. Starter kits are available in English or Spanish for adults and children under age 18.

The online Application for Benefits also includes links to information that will help you complete the form.

### If Your Application Is Denied

After we review your application and the information you provided, we may decide you do not meet the qualifications for disability benefits.

If you disagree with our decision, you have the right to ask us to look at your application again. The notice you receive from us that says you don't qualify will explain how to appeal our decision and the time period in which you must make the request.

If we decide you don't qualify:

- Because you are not disabled under our rules, you can appeal our decision online.

The online disability report will ask you for updated information about your medical condition and any treatment, tests, or doctor visits since we made our decision.

Appeal Medical Decision

- For non-medical reasons, you can appeal our decision online.

Appeal Other Decision

You also may call our toll-free number at **1-800-772-1213** to request an appeal. People who are deaf or hard of hearing can call our toll-free TTY number, 1-800-325-0778.

People who don't have enough work credits to be eligible for Social Security Disability benefits may possibly qualify for Supplemental Security Income (SSI) if they have limited income and resources.

For more information, please read "Your income and resources" on page 5 of our Supplemental Security Income (SSI) booklet.

## Benefits Planner: Disability \| How You Apply

You should apply for disability benefits as soon as you become disabled. If you are ready to apply now, you can:

- Complete your application online.
- Call our toll-free telephone number **1-800-772-1213**. If you are deaf or hard of hearing, you can call us at TTY **1-800-325-0778**.
- Call or visit your local Social Security office.

If you want to apply in person, please call and make an appointment **before** you visit your local office.

If you wish to help another person apply for disability benefits, please read .

### Information You Need To Apply

Here is the kind of information you should have:

### Information About You

- Your Social Security number and proof of your age;
- Names, addresses, and phone numbers of doctors, caseworkers, hospitals, and clinics that took care of you and the dates of your visits;
- Names and dosages of all the medications you are taking;
- Medical records from your doctors, therapists, hospitals, clinics, and caseworkers, that you already have in your possession;
- Laboratory and test results;
- A summary of where you worked and the kind of work you did; and
- Your most recent W-2 form or, if you were self-employed, a copy of your federal tax return.

### Information About Family Members

- Social Security numbers and proof of age for each family member who may qualify for benefits; and
- Proof of marriage, if your spouse is applying for benefits, as well as dates of prior marriages, if applicable.

The documents you may need to show us must be original documents or copies certified by the issuing office. You can mail or bring them to Social Security. We will make photocopies and return your original documents.

If you don't have all the documents you need, don't delay filing for benefits. We will help you get the information you need.

### More Help For Filing Your Claim

Our Disability Starter Kit will help you get ready for your disability interview or online application. Starter kits are available in English or Spanish for adults and children under age 18.

The online Application for Benefits also includes links to information that will help you complete the form.

### If Your Application Is Denied

After we review your application and the information you provided, we may decide you do not meet the qualifications for disability benefits.

If you disagree with our decision, you have the right to ask us to look at your application again. The notice you receive from us that says you don't qualify will explain how to appeal our decision and the time period in which you must make the request.

If we decide you don't qualify:

- Because you are not disabled under our rules, you can appeal our decision online.

The online disability report will ask you for updated information about your medical condition and any treatment, tests, or doctor visits since we made our decision.

Appeal Medical Decision

- For non-medical reasons, you can appeal our decision online.

Appeal Other Decision

You also may call our toll-free number at **1-800-772-1213** to request an appeal. People who are deaf or hard of hearing can call our toll-free TTY number, 1-800-325-0778.

People who don't have enough work credits to be eligible for Social Security Disability benefits may possibly qualify for Supplemental Security Income (SSI) if they have limited income and resources.

For more information, please read "Your income and resources" on page 5 of our Supplemental Security Income (SSI) booklet.

以下问题和答案涉及一些可能增加您福利的生活变化。

您的配偶或前配偶是否已去世？

您是否正在领取基于您自己工作记录的医疗保险福利，其中包括至少10年您缴纳社会保障税的收入 ？

如果您年满65岁，您可能有资格基于自己的记录领取现金福利。如果您已达到完全退休年龄或以上 ，无论您赚多少钱，您都可以工作并领取每月的社会保障福利。请查阅本出版物以了解更多信息。

您那个曾帮助抚养您的成年子女是否已去世？

如果您的子女有足够的工作积分，并且曾提供您至少一半的生活费，您可能有资格基于他或她的工 作记录获得更高的父母福利。

您是否正在领取基于您配偶工作记录的社会保障福利？

如果您工作过，您可能有资格基于自己的工作记录获得更高的退休福利。

您是否正在领取基于您父母工作记录的社会保障福利？

如果您工作过，您可能有资格基于自己的工作记录获得更高的残疾福利。

您目前是否未婚，但曾结婚10年或以上？

如果您年满62岁且未婚，并且那段婚姻持续了10年或以上，您可能有资格基于前配偶的工作记录获 得福利。

您的子女是否有资格根据您配偶的工作情况领取社会保障子女福利？

如果您照顾的子女未满16岁或在22岁之前残疾，您可能有资格领取配偶福利。

您目前是否正在领取退休或残疾福利，并且照顾的子女未满18岁或残疾？

您的子女可能根据您的工作情况有资格领取福利。

您是否正在领取补充保障收入（SSI）或社会保障福利，并且有服兵役经历？

您是否正在领取补充保障收入（SSI），并且您的父母一方已故或正在领取社会保障福利？

如果您未婚且未满18岁或在22岁之前残疾，并且您的父母一方已故或正在领取社会保障福利，您可 能有资格根据您父母的工作情况领取子女福利。

您的收入是否下降或您是否经历了财务资源的损失？

您可能能够通过补充保障收入计划获得额外收入，该计划帮助收入和财务资源有限的老年人和残疾 人。

## Benefits Planner: Retirement

### Benefits For Your Spouse

Even if you have never worked under Social Security, you may be able to get spouse s retirement benefits if you are at least 62 years of age and your spouse is receiving retirement or disability benefits. You can also qualify for Medicare at age 65.

If you are divorced, you may still be able to get benefits on your ex-spouse's record. For information on the requirements for Divorced Spouse's Benefits, read "If You Are Divorced

You can receive the spouse's benefit no matter what your age is if you are caring for their child who is also receiving benefits.

### How Much Will I Receive?

If you qualify and apply for your own retirement benefits and for benefits as a spouse, we always pay your own benefits first. If your benefits as a spouse are higher than your own retirement benefits, you will get a combination of benefits equaling the higher spouse benefit.

Your benefits as a spouse do not include any delayed retirement credits your spouse may receive.

If you begin receiving benefits:

- between age 62 and your full retirement age, the amount will be permanently reduced by a percentage based on the number of months up to your full retirement age.

 

- If you are under full retirement age and you continue to work while receiving benefits, your benefits may be affected by the retirement earnings test.

- at your full retirement age, your benefit as a spouse cannot exceed one-half of your spouse's full retirement amount.

 

- If you were born before January 2, 1954 and have already reached full retirement age, you can choose to receive only the spouse s benefit and delay receiving your retirement benefit until a later date. If your spouse is full retirement age and applying for spouse s benefits only, they can apply online by using the retirement application. Your spouse can also contact us to schedule an appointment.

If your spouse s birthday is January 2, 1954 or later, the option to take only one benefit at full retirement age no longer exists. If your spouse files for one benefit, they will be effectively filing for all retirement or spousal benefits.

If you will receive a pension for work not covered by Social Security such as government employment, the amount of your Social Security benefits on your spouse's record may be reduced.

Benefits paid to you as a spouse will not decrease your spouse s retirement benefit. In fact, the value of the benefits you may receive, added to their benefits, may help your spouse decide if taking benefits sooner may be more advantageous.

#### Maximum Family Benefits

If one of your spouse's children also qualifies for benefits, there is a limit to the amount we can pay family members.

The total depends on your spouse's benefit amount and the number of family members who also qualify on the same record. The total varies, but generally the total amount the worker (your spouse) and their family members can receive is about 150 to 180 percent of the worker's full retirement benefit.

If there is an ex-spouse who also qualifies for benefits, they will not affect the total amount of benefits you or your family may receive.

### How Do I Apply?

You can apply:

- Online - Use our Social Security Retirement/Medicare Benefit Application to apply for retirement, spouse's, divorced spouse's or Medicare benefits.

 

- If your spouse is already receiving benefits when you apply, or if you and your spouse apply at the same time, we will also check your eligibility for benefits as a spouse. If you qualify, your application will automatically serve as a request for spousal benefits.

- By phone - Call us at 1-800-772-1213. If you are deaf or hard of hearing, you can call us at TTY 1-800-325-0778.

 

- In person - Visit your local Social Security office. (Call first to make an appointment.)

- If you do not live in the U.S. or one of its territories you can also - Contact the nearest U.S. Social Security office, U.S. Embassy or consulate.

### Next Steps

Even if you do not qualify for benefits on someone else's record, some members of your family may qualify for benefits on your record. If you:

- are interested in information about benefits for your family, go to "Benefits For Your Family."

- never married or had children, go to "How You Apply For Retirement Benefits Or Medicare.""}, {"chunk_id": "Benefits Planner: Retirement | Benefits For Your Spouse | Social Security Administration#2_0::c0000", "text": "# Benefits Planner: Retirement | Benefits For Your Spouse | Social Security Administration

Just as you plan for your family's protection if you die, you should consider the Social Security benefits that may be available if you are the survivor that is, the spouse, child, or parent of a worker who dies. That person must have worked long enough under Social Security to qualify for benefits.

A worker can earn up to four credits each year. In 2019, for example, your spouse can earn one credit for each $1,360 of wages or self-employment income. When your spouse has earned $5,440, they have earned their four credits for the year.

We should be notified as soon as possible when a person dies. However, you cannot report a death or apply for survivors benefits online.

## Benefits Planner: Retirement

### Benefits For Your Spouse

Even if you have never worked under Social Security, you may be able to get spouse s retirement benefits if you are at least 62 years of age and your spouse is receiving retirement or disability benefits. You can also qualify for Medicare at age 65.

If you are divorced, you may still be able to get benefits on your ex-spouse's record. For information on the requirements for Divorced Spouse's Benefits, read "If You Are Divorced

You can receive the spouse's benefit no matter what your age is if you are caring for their child who is also receiving benefits.

### How Much Will I Receive?

If you qualify and apply for your own retirement benefits and for benefits as a spouse, we always pay your own benefits first. If your benefits as a spouse are higher than your own retirement benefits, you will get a combination of benefits equaling the higher spouse benefit.

Your benefits as a spouse do not include any delayed retirement credits your spouse may receive.

If you begin receiving benefits:

- between age 62 and your full retirement age, the amount will be permanently reduced by a percentage based on the number of months up to your full retirement age.

 

- If you are under full retirement age and you continue to work while receiving benefits, your benefits may be affected by the retirement earnings test.

- at your full retirement age, your benefit as a spouse cannot exceed one-half of your spouse's full retirement amount.

 

- If you were born before January 2, 1954 and have already reached full retirement age, you can choose to receive only the spouse s benefit and delay receiving your retirement benefit until a later date. If your spouse is full retirement age and applying for spouse s benefits only, they can apply online by using the retirement application. Your spouse can also contact us to schedule an appointment.

If your spouse s birthday is January 2, 1954 or later, the option to take only one benefit at full retirement age no longer exists. If your spouse files for one benefit, they will be effectively filing for all retirement or spousal benefits.

If you will receive a pension for work not covered by Social Security such as government employment, the amount of your Social Security benefits on your spouse's record may be reduced.

Benefits paid to you as a spouse will not decrease your spouse s retirement benefit. In fact, the value of the benefits you may receive, added to their benefits, may help your spouse decide if taking benefits sooner may be more advantageous.

#### Maximum Family Benefits

If one of your spouse's children also qualifies for benefits, there is a limit to the amount we can pay family members.

The total depends on your spouse's benefit amount and the number of family members who also qualify on the same record. The total varies, but generally the total amount the worker (your spouse) and their family members can receive is about 150 to 180 percent of the worker's full retirement benefit.

If there is an ex-spouse who also qualifies for benefits, they will not affect the total amount of benefits you or your family may receive.

### How Do I Apply?

You can apply:

- Online - Use our Social Security Retirement/Medicare Benefit Application to apply for retirement, spouse's, divorced spouse's or Medicare benefits.

 

- If your spouse is already receiving benefits when you apply, or if you and your spouse apply at the same time, we will also check your eligibility for benefits as a spouse. If you qualify, your application will automatically serve as a request for spousal benefits.

- By phone - Call us at 1-800-772-1213. If you are deaf or hard of hearing, you can call us at TTY 1-800-325-0778.

 

- In person - Visit your local Social Security office. (Call first to make an appointment.)

- If you do not live in the U.S. or one of its territories you can also - Contact the nearest U.S. Social Security office, U.S. Embassy or consulate.

### Next Steps

Even if you do not qualify for benefits on someone else's record, some members of your family may qualify for benefits on your record. If you:

- are interested in information about benefits for your family, go to "Benefits For Your Family."

- never married or had children, go to "How You Apply For Retirement Benefits Or Medicare.""}, {"chunk_id": "Benefits Planner: Retirement | Benefits For Your Spouse | Social Security Administration#2_0::c0000", "text": "# Benefits Planner: Retirement | Benefits For Your Spouse | Social Security Administration

Just as you plan for your family's protection if you die, you should consider the Social Security benefits that may be available if you are the survivor that is, the spouse, child, or parent of a worker who dies. That person must have worked long enough under Social Security to qualify for benefits.

A worker can earn up to four credits each year. In 2019, for example, your spouse can earn one credit for each $1,360 of wages or self-employment income. When your spouse has earned $5,440, they have earned their four credits for the year.

The number of credits needed to provide benefits for survivors depends on the worker's age when they die. We should be notified as soon as possible when a person dies. However, you cannot report a death or apply for survivors benefits online.

In most cases, the funeral home will report the person s death to us. You should give the funeral home the deceased person s Social Security number if you want them to make the report.

# Request a Board Appeal

选择此选项时，您将向位于华盛顿特区的Veterans' Appeals委员会的Veterans Law Judge提出上诉。熟悉Veterans法律的法官将审查您的案件。

您也可以选择请求与法官举行听证会，可以在华盛顿特区亲自出席，或通过视频会议在您附近的VA地点进行。

### 我可以请求Board Appeal吗？

在初始索赔、Supplemental Claim或Higher-Level Review决定之后，您可以请求Board Appeal。您不能连续请求两次Board Appeal。

## 我可以添加新证据吗？

您可以选择添加新证据供法官审查。您需要在VA收到您的Board Appeal表格之日起90天内提交此证据。

此选项将花费更长时间。

## 我可以请求听证会吗？

您可以选择请求与法官举行听证会。视频会议听证会将在您附近的VA地点进行。

此选项将花费更长时间。

## 听证会上会发生什么？

您和法官将进行对话。法官将听取您的证词，并可能问您几个问题。如果您有代表，您的代表可以在听证会上帮助您。

听证会将被记录并添加到您的上诉文件中。您可以在听证会后90天内添加新的相关证据，但这不是必需的。

## 如何请求Board Appeal？

要请求Board Appeal，请填写Decision Review Request: Board Appeal (VA Form 10182)。下载VA Form 10182 (PDF)

1.  ### 从3个选项中选择1个，向 Veterans Law Judge 提出上诉

Direct Review 如果你希望 Veterans Law Judge 尽快审查你的案件，请选择 Direct Review。

你不能提交任何证据。

约1年 Board 对无新证据且无听证的上诉作出裁决的目标时间约为一年。

Evidence Submission 如果你有其他证据供 Veterans Law Judge 审查，请选择 Evidence Submission。

你必须在 VA 收到你的 Board Appeal 表格之日起90天内提交证据。

更长 如果你添加新证据，所需时间将比 Direct Review 上诉选项更长。

Hearing Request 如果你希望在附近的 VA 地点与 Veterans Law Judge 进行视频会议听证，请选择 Hearing Request。

在听证会上，你和 Veterans Law Judge 将进行对话，他们会询问你关于上诉的问题。你的听证将被记录并添加到你的上诉档案中。了解更多关于听证会以及如何申请的信息

你可以在听证后90天内添加新的相关证据，但这不是必需的。

更长 如果你要求听证，所需时间将比 Direct Review 上诉选项更长。

2.  ### 在 Part III 中列出你希望上诉的问题

你可以包括 VA 已决定的所有或部分问题。你需要列出你不同意的每个问题及对应的 VA 决定日期。

3.  ### 申请

填写 Decision Review Request: Board Appeal (VA Form 10182)。下载 VA Form 10182 (PDF)

邮寄

将填写完整的表格发送至以下地址：

Board of Veterans Appeals PO Box 27063 Washington, D.C. 20038

亲自办理

将填写完毕的表格带到地区福利办公室。查找离您最近的地区福利办公室

传真办理

将填写完毕的表格传真至 844-678-8979。

您也可以向地区福利办公室索取此表格的副本进行填写。或者，您可以拨打 VA 免费热线 800-827-1000（周一至周五，东部时间上午 8:00 至晚上 9:00）索取表格。

#### 标记您的日历

您有 1 年的时间（自决定日期起）来申请 Board Appeal。如果您是共同申领同一福利的多人之一（这种情况很少见），则您有 60 天的时间。

## Board 决定之后

如果您不同意 Board 的决定，并且有支持您案件的新且相关的证据，您可以提交 Supplemental Claim。您也可以向 U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims 提出上诉。了解 Board 决定后您的更多选择

# VA 决策复核与上诉

如果您不同意 VA 的决策，您可以选择以下复核选项之一来继续您的案件。如果您对该复核结果不满意，您可以尝试另一个选项。

#### 标记您的日历

您有自决策日期起 1 年的时间来请求决策复核，除非您有 fiduciary claim 或 multiple party claim。请查看这些罕见情况是否适用于您

## 决策复核选项

- 添加新的且相关的证据（提交 Supplemental Claim）
- 请求高级审阅员重新审查（请求 Higher-Level Review）
- 向 Veterans Law Judge 上诉（请求 Board Appeal）

### 添加新的且相关的证据

下载 VA Form 20-0995：Supplemental Claim（PDF）

当您选择提交 Supplemental Claim 时，您是在添加支持您案件的新证据或指明需要审查的证据。审阅员将查看所有证据并确定是否改变决策。了解如何提交 Supplemental Claim

您必须提交 VA 之前没有的、支持您案件的证据。

4-5 个月 VA 完成 Supplemental Claims 的目标是 125 天。

#### 我可以提交 Supplemental Claim 吗？

如果您有新证据，您可以在决策后 1 年内提交 Supplemental Claim。

但如果您有 fiduciary claim 或您是多个声称同一福利的人之一（这种情况很少见），则不能提交 Supplemental Claim。请查看这些罕见情况是否适用于您

### 请求高级审阅员重新审查

下载 VA Form 20-0996：Higher-Level Review（PDF）

当您选择请求 Higher-Level Review 时，您是在请求对相同证据进行另一次审查。高级审阅员将重新审查您的案件，并确定是否可以根据意见分歧或 VA 犯下的错误来更改决策。了解如何请求 Higher-Level Review

您无法提交任何证据。

您和/或您的代表可以通过电话与审核员沟通。您可以告诉他们为什么您认为决定应被更改，并指出错误。

4-5个月 VA完成Higher-Level Reviews的目标是125天。如果VA需要获取记录或安排新的考试以纠正错误，审核可能需要更长时间。

#### 我可以申请Higher-Level Review吗？

您可以对初始申请或Supplemental Claim决定申请Higher-Level Review。在Higher-Level Review或Board Appeal之后，此选项不可用。

### 向Veterans Law Judge上诉

## 如何请求Board Appeal？

1.  ### 从3个选项中选择1个，向 Veterans Law Judge 提出上诉

Direct Review 如果你希望 Veterans Law Judge 尽快审查你的案件，请选择 Direct Review。

你不能提交任何证据。

约1年 Board 对无新证据且无听证的上诉作出裁决的目标时间约为一年。

Evidence Submission 如果你有其他证据供 Veterans Law Judge 审查，请选择 Evidence Submission。

你必须在 VA 收到你的 Board Appeal 表格之日起90天内提交证据。

更长 如果你添加新证据，所需时间将比 Direct Review 上诉选项更长。

Hearing Request 如果你希望在附近的 VA 地点与 Veterans Law Judge 进行视频会议听证，请选择 Hearing Request。

在听证会上，你和 Veterans Law Judge 将进行对话，他们会询问你关于上诉的问题。你的听证将被记录并添加到你的上诉档案中。了解更多关于听证会以及如何申请的信息

你可以在听证后90天内添加新的相关证据，但这不是必需的。

3.  ### 申请

填写 Decision Review Request: Board Appeal (VA Form 10182)。下载 VA Form 10182 (PDF)

## Veterans Group Life Insurance (VGLI)

With Veterans Group Life Insurance (VGLI), you may be able to keep your life insurance coverage after you leave the military for as long as you continue to pay the premiums. Find out if you qualify for VGLI and how to manage your coverage.

## Am I eligible for Veterans Group Life Insurance?

You may be able to get VGLI if you meet at least one of the requirements listed below.

## At least one of these must be true. You:

Had part-time Servicemembers Group Life Insurance (SGLI) as a member of the National Guard or Reserves, and you suffered an injury or disability (damage to your body or mind that makes it hard for you to do everyday tasks, including meaningful work) while on duty including direct traveling to and from duty that disqualified you for standard premium insurance rates, or Had SGLI while you were in the military and you re within 1 year and 120 days of being released from an active-duty period of 31 or more days, or Are within 1 year and 120 days of retiring or being released from the Ready Reserves or National Guard, or Are within 1 year and 120 days of assignment to the Individual Ready Reserves (IRR) of a branch of service, or to the Inactive National Guard (ING). This includes members of the United States Public Health Service Inactive Reserve Corps (IRC), or Are within 1 year and 120 days of being put on the Temporary Disability Retirement List (TDRL)

## Who s covered?

## Veterans Former service members

## What life insurance benefits can I get with VGLI?

$10,000 to $400,000 in life insurance benefits, based on the amount of SGLI coverage you had when you left the military.

Note: When you leave the military, you can sign up through VGLI for coverage up to the amount you had through SGLI. You can also increase your coverage by $25,000 every 5 years up to $400,000 until you re 60 years old.

## How do I get these benefits?

You ll need to apply for VGLI within one year and 120 days of leaving the military.

If you sign up within 240 days of leaving the military, you won t need to prove you re in good health. If you sign up after the 240-day period, you ll need to submit evidence that you re in good health.

## Apply in one of these ways:

Apply through the Office of Servicemembers Group Life Insurance (OSGLI), using the Prudential website. Apply online through OSGLI Apply online through eBenefits Apply by mail or fax. Fill out the Application for Veterans Group Life Insurance (SGLV 8714). Download the Application for Veterans Group Life Insurance (PDF)

## Fax the form to 800-236-6142, or mail it to:

## OSGLI PO Box 41618 Philadelphia, PA 19176-9913

To reinstate a VGLI policy that has expired, you ll need to fill out an Application for Reinstatement of VGLI Coverage (SGLV 180). Download SGLV 180 (PDF)

## How much will I pay for these benefits?

VGLI premium rates are based on your age and the amount of insurance coverage you want.

Choose your age to find monthly premium rates as of July 1, 2014.

## Can I choose or update my beneficiaries?

Yes. You can choose your beneficiaries (the people you pick to get the money from your life insurance policy if you die) and change them as needed.

## Update your beneficiary information in one of these ways:

Access your policy online. Find your policy through Prudential Life Insurance Company of America, or Fill out a VGLI Beneficiary Designation form (SGLV 8721). Download SGLV 8721 (PDF)

## Fax the form to 800-236-6142, or mail it to:

## OSGLI PO Box 41618 Philadelphia, PA 19176-9913

## Can I convert my VGLI policy into a commercial policy?

Yes. You can convert your policy into a commercial (civilian) policy at any time. You ll be able to convert at standard premium rates, without having to provide proof that you re in good health.

## To convert your VGLI policy:

## Choose your new insurance company.View our list of companies that take part in this program (PDF)

Apply at the local sales office of your chosen company.

Get a letter from OSGLI confirming that you have VGLI coverage (called a VGLI Conversion Notice) and give the letter to the agent who takes your application.

Note: The conversion policy must be a permanent policy, such as a whole life policy. You can t convert to other types of policies, like term, variable life, or universal life insurance. And supplementary policy benefits, like Accidental Death and Dismemberment or Waiver of Premium for Disability, aren t considered part of the conversion policy.

## Veterans Group Life Insurance (VGLI)

With Veterans Group Life Insurance (VGLI), you may be able to keep your life insurance coverage after you leave the military for as long as you continue to pay the premiums. Find out if you qualify for VGLI and how to manage your coverage.

## Am I eligible for Veterans Group Life Insurance?

You may be able to get VGLI if you meet at least one of the requirements listed below.

## At least one of these must be true. You:

Had part-time Servicemembers Group Life Insurance (SGLI) as a member of the National Guard or Reserves, and you suffered an injury or disability (damage to your body or mind that makes it hard for you to do everyday tasks, including meaningful work) while on duty including direct traveling to and from duty that disqualified you for standard premium insurance rates, or Had SGLI while you were in the military and you re within 1 year and 120 days of being released from an active-duty period of 31 or more days, or Are within 1 year and 120 days of retiring or being released from the Ready Reserves or National Guard, or Are within 1 year and 120 days of assignment to the Individual Ready Reserves (IRR) of a branch of service, or to the Inactive National Guard (ING). This includes members of the United States Public Health Service Inactive Reserve Corps (IRC), or Are within 1 year and 120 days of being put on the Temporary Disability Retirement List (TDRL)

## Who s covered?

## Veterans Former service members

## What life insurance benefits can I get with VGLI?

$10,000 to $400,000 in life insurance benefits, based on the amount of SGLI coverage you had when you left the military.

Note: When you leave the military, you can sign up through VGLI for coverage up to the amount you had through SGLI. You can also increase your coverage by $25,000 every 5 years up to $400,000 until you re 60 years old.

## How do I get these benefits?

You ll need to apply for VGLI within one year and 120 days of leaving the military.

If you sign up within 240 days of leaving the military, you won t need to prove you re in good health. If you sign up after the 240-day period, you ll need to submit evidence that you re in good health.

## Apply in one of these ways:

Apply through the Office of Servicemembers Group Life Insurance (OSGLI), using the Prudential website. Apply online through OSGLI Apply online through eBenefits Apply by mail or fax. Fill out the Application for Veterans Group Life Insurance (SGLV 8714). Download the Application for Veterans Group Life Insurance (PDF)

## Fax the form to 800-236-6142, or mail it to:

## OSGLI PO Box 41618 Philadelphia, PA 19176-9913

To reinstate a VGLI policy that has expired, you ll need to fill out an Application for Reinstatement of VGLI Coverage (SGLV 180). Download SGLV 180 (PDF)

## How much will I pay for these benefits?

VGLI premium rates are based on your age and the amount of insurance coverage you want.

Choose your age to find monthly premium rates as of July 1, 2014.

## Can I choose or update my beneficiaries?

Yes. You can choose your beneficiaries (the people you pick to get the money from your life insurance policy if you die) and change them as needed.

## Update your beneficiary information in one of these ways:

Access your policy online. Find your policy through Prudential Life Insurance Company of America, or Fill out a VGLI Beneficiary Designation form (SGLV 8721). Download SGLV 8721 (PDF)

## Fax the form to 800-236-6142, or mail it to:

## OSGLI PO Box 41618 Philadelphia, PA 19176-9913

## Can I convert my VGLI policy into a commercial policy?

Yes. You can convert your policy into a commercial (civilian) policy at any time. You ll be able to convert at standard premium rates, without having to provide proof that you re in good health.

## To convert your VGLI policy:

## Choose your new insurance company.View our list of companies that take part in this program (PDF)

Apply at the local sales office of your chosen company.

Get a letter from OSGLI confirming that you have VGLI coverage (called a VGLI Conversion Notice) and give the letter to the agent who takes your application.

Note: The conversion policy must be a permanent policy, such as a whole life policy. You can t convert to other types of policies, like term, variable life, or universal life insurance. And supplementary policy benefits, like Accidental Death and Dismemberment or Waiver of Premium for Disability, aren t considered part of the conversion policy.

If you have questions about Servicemembers or Veterans Group Life Insurance, you can call the Office of Servicemembers Group Life Insurance (OSGLI) at 800-419-1473 or email the Prudential Insurance Company.

### 我收到了DMV的保险“信函”或“命令”。我能做什么？

仔细阅读信函或命令（参见示例 [1]），迅速回复，并立即联系您的保险公司。如果有问题，您有责任解决。如果您不这样做，DMV可能会暂停您的车辆注册和驾驶执照。

#### 不要

- 如果您的保险被取消，即使您认为这是个错误，也不要使用您的车辆
- 在您与保险公司解决问题时，不要保留车牌 1

#### 要

- 在您的保险覆盖结束前，交出您的车辆注册和车牌 [2]

### 我如何回复信函或命令？

您的回复必须

- 证明您有保险覆盖
- 证明您出售了车辆
- 证明不需要保险覆盖

如果您有保险覆盖，也请您的保险公司（不要问您的代理人或经纪人）向DMV电子提交保险覆盖通知。 2

### 如果我没有责任保险，我必须做什么？

如果您没有保险，或者保险即将到期且您不打算更换，您需要立即向DMV交出您的车牌 [2]。 3

### 我收到一封说明我的保险失效的信。我能做什么？

这封信意味着您的保险公司通知DMV您的保险覆盖已结束，并且没有其他公司通知DMV关于新的覆盖。

如果您有保险，请按照信中的指示操作，并联系您的公司或代理人解决问题。请您的公司向DMV电子提交覆盖通知。

如果您没有保险，您需要立即向DMV交出您的车辆注册和车牌。

### 我收到一封说明我的驾照被暂停的信。我能做什么？

这封信意味着您的保险公司已通知DMV您的保险保障已终止，且没有其他公司就新保障通知DMV。

如果您有保险，请按照信中的指示操作，并就问题联系您的公司或代理人。请您的公司以电子方式向DMV提交保障通知。

如果您没有保险，您需要立即将车辆登记和车牌交还给DMV。

当保障中断达到91天或以上，或中断期间尚未确定时，驾驶执照将被吊销。要确定中断期间，

- 车牌必须交还，或
- 车牌必须报告为丢失/被盗/被没收，或
- 登记必须到期，或
- 车牌必须由DMV转移到另一辆车，或
- DMV必须收到新的或恢复的保险证明，或
- DMV必须收到其他可接受的证明

一旦中断期间确定，登记将被暂停，如果中断期间为91天或以上，您的驾驶执照也将被暂停相同天数。暂停可能不在同一日期生效。因此，您可能先执行驾驶执照的暂停，或先执行登记的暂停。驾驶执照的暂停不会结束，直到您支付暂停终止费[3]并执行完暂停。

- 1. 将您的车牌交还给DMV。当问题纠正后，您可以获得您的登记和新车牌。
